- Apps on their own can bring their data over from Pulse: on the first start (setup screen) a Bring my data button asks Pulse (it hands over that app's settings and files through a provider only apps signed with the same key can read) and takes them in; Pulse keeps its own copy. Needs Pulse 2.0.37 or newer on the phone.
- Apps on their own are smaller: each one leaves out the assets and native libraries only other apps use, and the launcher entries and components of the other apps, so the shrinker can drop what is left unused. Pulse Calculator is now a lean app of its own (Compose and the calculator only: a few MB instead of the 40 MB of the whole of Pulse; Material and AMOLED looks).
- More apps on their own are lean (a few MB each instead of 40 MB): Calculator, TempMail, Browser, Voice Recorder; an app whose lean build fails is still built the old way, so none is lost.
- Messages: the "Blocked (n)" line at the top of the list is gone (it took room); Settings > Blocked numbers has a button to read their messages.
- Files: the bookmarked folders no longer sit as a row of chips at the top of Browse by default (they are in the menu); Settings > Drawer > "Bookmarks above the list" turns the row on.
- Crash fix (#27, Android 10): InputStream.readNBytes is Android 13+; replaced with readUpTo() in Files preview, LinkFinder, GameHub art. New scripts/check_api.py flags such calls (readNBytes, readAllBytes, transferTo, List.of, Files.readString ...) and runs in check_imports.py and in CI before the build.
- Lazy lists: scripts/check_lazy.py lists LazyColumn keys that can repeat (crash 'Key was already used') and lazy lists inside verticalScroll; link/history/dir lists in Downloads, Share, Files search, Debloat, Files home now use distinct().
- Toolkit: the coin flip and the dice are quicker (coin 2-3 turns in 0.75 s, dice 0.8 s) and land with a snap instead of a long slow stop; the Quick Settings dice/coin tiles spin their pictures twice, faster, then settle.
- Lean (small) apps: they now use Pulse's real look system (Windows 95 / XP / 7 / 10 / 11, Material, AMOLED, One UI, ColorOS and the glass looks) instead of the single Material stand-in: the look files are copied from the Pulse source at build time (lean/build.gradle.kts, leanLook), the look is chosen per app (Material by default) from the app's look row. The 95 / XP / 7 bitmap icon packs are not inside them (the vector icons are drawn). Never compiled: if the lean build fails the workflow falls back to the whole-Pulse build.
